subject: humanities
passage: Commedia dell'arte, a popular form of theater in sixteenth-century Italy, did not use full written scripts. Troupes worked from a short outline of the plot that was often pinned up backstage. Each actor played the same masked character for years and knew that character's jokes and habits well, so performers could ______ their dialogue on the spot, changing it to suit each audience.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The troupes had no "full written scripts," only a plot outline, and actors made up their lines "on the spot" to suit each audience. Making something up in the moment is improvising, so "improvise" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. With no full scripts, there were no written lines to memorize, and the dialogue changed "on the spot."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text involves changing words from one language into another.
explanation.C: Correct. Actors who knew their characters well could invent, or improvise, their lines on the spot from a plot outline.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how loudly actors spoke; it is about where their words came from.
